subject: Dedicated capacity recommendation — Hyperion POC: H100 vs A100 vs L4 tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@hyperion.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Hyperion POC — Dedicated capacity sketch (H100/A100/L4)

Hi Sarah,

Thanks again for the sync this week. As requested, attached is a concise sketch of how we might size Dedicated capacity for your proof-of-concept (3-month POC) and a short note on SKU tradeoffs. The attached spreadsheet contains the per-workload pod counts I used to derive throughput. High-level summary below so we can iterate quickly: 

- Fast inference for short chat queries (<= 4k tokens): L4 is cost-effective and handles high QPS with low latency.
- Long-context and multimodal models (>= 16k context, embeddings for indexing): H100 (80GB) preferred for KV cache & large-batch throughput.
- Mid-range models where memory but not max throughput is needed: A100 40GB can be a balanced option if you expect fewer long sequences but higher concurrency.

Key tradeoffs we highlighted in the spreadsheet:
- Memory ceiling: H100 supports larger KV caches and longer context without offloading. If you plan to run >2x 32k-context generations per second, H100 is materially better.
- Per-GPU concurrency: L4 can handle many small requests concurrently and is cheaper per-hour, but saturates quickly with very long contexts.
- Quantization: Running 8-bit/4-bit quantized weights on A100/L4 increases throughput and allows smaller pods; H100 still retains advantage for unquantized/FP16 for throughput-sensitive models.

Proposed initial Dedicated pool for POC (conservative):
- 8x L4 nodes for chat/front-door routing (short-form prompts)
- 4x A100 40GB nodes for mid-range transformer variants and batched embeddings
- 2x H100 80GB nodes reserved for long-context, repro runtime with heavy KV cache use

I flagged options in the spreadsheet to shift 2 L4 -> A100 if you expect heavy batched offline embeddings. Estimated kickoff cost & ops notes are in the PDF.

Please review and let me know what capacity profile matches your expected 95th percentile concurrency. Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the numbers.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few quick clarifying questions before we lock things down:

1) For our vector DB ingestion pipeline we'll be streaming 1M short documents initially, with peak embedding batch jobs overnight. Do you recommend those jobs run against A100 or L4? Cost vs throughput tradeoff seems non-linear in the sheet.

2) On H100: can the 2 nodes handle model variants with 32k context + large KV cache if we run 2 concurrent sessions? Our repo has a few heavy rerank flows that may pin memory.

3) We have a security ask around data residency for logs — can Dedicated pools be colocated in our VPC with our EU region later in the program?

Also: can you send a suggested mutual action plan for the POC milestones tied to those capacity choices?

—Sarah

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Hyperion POC — Dedicated capacity sketch (H100/A100/L4)

Quick internal notes to align the response:

Ben — draft answers below, please refine and send to Sarah. Dev, can you validate the A100 vs L4 batch numbers and the KV cache sizing assumptions in the sheet? Specifically:

- Embedding batch jobs: L4 gives better $/sec for small models but A100 amortizes better for very large batches (>= 8k sequences per batch) because of FP16 matmul advantages. Recommend we propose: 
  - Run overnight high-throughput embeddings on A100 (2 nodes) for the POC run to finish within the maintenance window.
  - Keep L4 for the daytime inference front-door.

- H100 capacity: Dev to confirm, but current benchmarks indicate a single H100 80GB can host 1x 32k context generation with KV cache comfortably; two concurrent sessions may push memory and require either:
  - model quantization to 8-bit + KV cache trimming, or
  - pin the second session to A100 with offload for less than 50 tokens/sec sustained.

- Residency/VPC: Yes — Dedicated pools can be provisioned in a customer VPC in our supported regions. For EU residency we'll need to plan the Private control plane or an EU-hosted Dedicated cluster; cost and lead time differ. Marissa, please add timeline/ops note for EU colocations in the MOP PDF.

Action items before sending to customer:
- Dev: validate the batch thresholds and provide a short note we can include in email (2–3 bullet explanation).
- Marissa: add EU VPC bullet & expected provisioning lead time to the MOP.
- Ben: update spreadsheet to reflect the overnight A100 plan and call out fallback policy if H100 memory is saturated.

If that looks good I'll ok a one-time POC discount (internal approval pending) and include the mutual action plan.

—Olga
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Apr 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Hyperion POC — Dedicated capacity sketch (H100/A100/L4)

Ben / Olga / Marissa — validated the numbers in the spreadsheet and added a short technical note (attached to the Drive link). Summary:

- Embedding jobs: recommend A100 for batch sizes >= 8k. Benchmarks show ~2.8x throughput vs L4 at those batch sizes when using FP16. For many smaller batches (<= 2k) L4 is cheaper and has lower cold-start latency.

- H100 concurrency: two concurrent 32k-context generations are borderline on 80GB H100 without quantization. If Hyperion wants 2x concurrent heavy sessions we recommend:
  1) Reserve 2 H100 but set an autoscaling buffer and fallback to an A100 pool for the second session when KV cache pressure is high.
  2) Or run 1x H100 (primary long-context) + 1x A100 with offload shim for lower-priority long runs.

- Quantization tradeoffs: 8-bit/LLM.int8-like paths reduce memory footprint ~30–40% and improve throughput on A100 and L4 but may produce small accuracy delta on some rerank models. We'll propose a quick eval to show quality delta on Hyperion's rerank tasks before recommending aggressive quantization.

- Ops/Provisioning: EU VPC Dedicated requires 6–8 weeks lead time for Reserved setup and IAM/KMS integration.

I updated the spreadsheet: added columns for "recommended host for overnight embeddings" and "fallback policy for H100 saturation". Ben — you can attach that and the MOP PDF to the reply.

Cheers,
Dev
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the questions and the patience. Per Olga and Dev's notes (summary below) we propose the following mutual action plan and capacity mapping for the 3-month POC: 

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- Week 0 (contract & capacity provisioning): Provision Dedicated pool in US (will provide an EU timeline if you want locality). Estimated lead time 2–3 weeks for US Dedicated.
- Week 1 (model onboarding & small-scale eval): Run quantization and quality checks on your rerank models (Dev will run the eval).
- Week 2–3 (ingestion & embeddings): Run overnight embedding batches on A100 nodes; daytime inference on L4.
- Week 4 (load test & SLO tuning): Execute 95th/99th percentile load tests, tune batching & cache TTLs.
- Month 2–3 (stabilization & handoff): Evaluate cost/perf, decide on steady-state fleet mix and any scaling to EU.

Recommended Dedicated pool (POC):
- 8x L4 nodes — daytime chat & front-door (low latency, high concurrency).
- 4x A100 40GB nodes — batched embeddings & mid-size models (overnight heavy jobs).
- 2x H100 80GB nodes — reserved for long-context, high-memory sessions; set autoscale buffer to spin up extra A100 if sustained concurrency >1.

Fallback policy: If H100 KV cache pressure >80% for >5 minutes, route lower-priority long jobs to A100 with offload and notify on-call.

Security & residency: We can provision the Dedicated pool in your VPC; EU residency will require Private control-plane or EU-hosted Dedicated cluster (6–8 weeks).

Attachments: mutual action plan and the updated spreadsheet & MOP are in the Drive link. Please reply with approval or any changes and we will move to a firm provisioning schedule.

If you want a quick call tomorrow to finalize, I can do 10:00–11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
